study_identification_part.si4_title: Individualized gray matter morphological abnormalities unveil two neuroanatomical obsessive-compulsive disorder subtypes

study_characteristics_part.sc1_study_objective: Identify OCD subtypes using individualized deviations from normative models of regional gray matter volume (GMV), test reproducibility, and examine associations with brain network architecture and neurotransmitter receptor/transporter distributions.

rci1_dataset_name.answer: Local Community Cohort; Southwest University Adult Lifespan Dataset
rci1_dataset_name.reason: The paper explicitly states that 106 healthy controls were recruited from the community for the primary analysis and that a separate dataset (Southwest University Adult Lifespan Dataset, from reference [46]) was used to construct the normal structural covariance network.
rci1_dataset_name.supporting_text: Healthy controls (HCs, n = 106) were enlisted from the community via poster advertisements.; The normal structural covariance network was constructed using another extensive dataset from a single site, comprising 492 healthy individuals aged 19 -80 years. Further details about this dataset are available elsewhere [46].

clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa8_key_findings_brief: Identified two robust OCD subtypes with opposite GMV deviation patterns relative to HCs; distinct disease epicenters (subtype 1: middle frontal gyrus; subtype 2: striatum/thalamus/hippocampus) and distinct associations with neurotransmitter receptors (e.g., 5HT1A for subtype 1; 5HT2A for subtype 2).
